concept.name: Aroon up
concept.definition: Tushar Chande's 1995 indicator measuring how recently price made a new n-period high, expressed as a 0-100 percentage: 100 when the high occurred in the current period, decaying toward 0 as it recedes into the past.
concept.intuition: Instead of asking how far price moved, Aroon-Up asks how long ago the latest high was - frequent new highs keep it pinned near 100.
concept.mechanics: Aroon-Up = 100 x (n - periods since the n-period high) / n, default n = 25. Readings above 50 mean a new high within the most recent half of the window; sustained 70-100 readings mark strong uptrends.
concept.failure_modes: It measures time, not magnitude - a market drifting sideways near its highs keeps Aroon-Up high without real momentum, and the reading decays mechanically as the window ages even when price is flat.
concept.misconceptions: Aroon-Up at 100 does not mean 'overbought, expect reversal' - it only means the latest n-period high happened today.
concept.example: With n = 25 and the 25-day high made 5 days ago: Aroon-Up = (25-5)/25 x 100 = 80.
